text: Centroid-anchored labels (names, ISO codes flag emoji), ggrepel collision avoidance available. Zoom zoom_map(), takes longitude latitude limits keeps map’s projection: adding coord_quickmap(xlim, ylim) replace projection unprojected one.
code: mapdf <- attach_geometry(   dplyr::filter(snap, continent == "Europe"), geometry = "polygon" ) (world_map(mapdf, gdp_per_capita) +    geom_country_labels(repel = FALSE, size = 2.5)) |>   zoom_map(xlim = c(-25, 45), ylim = c(34, 72))

title: Beyond the choropleth
text: remaining displays follow one-call pattern require optional packages, shown code:
code: # Bivariate choropleth (two variables at once): needs `biscale` + `sf` world_data(2020, c(gdp = "NY.GDP.PCAP.KD", life = "SP.DYN.LE00.IN"),            geometry = "sf") |>   bivariate_map(gdp, life)  # Area-honest cartogram: needs `cartogram` + `sf` world_data(2020, c(pop = "SP.POP.TOTL"), geometry = "sf") |>   cartogram_map(pop, type = "dorling")  # The same Dorling cartogram as a first-class verb, with its tuning exposed world_data(2020, c(pop = "SP.POP.TOTL"), geometry = "sf") |>   dorling_map(pop, k = 4)  # The fast flow-based cartogram (Gastner-Seguy-More): needs `cartogramR` world_data(2020, c(pop = "SP.POP.TOTL"), geometry = "sf") |>   cartogram_map(pop, type = "flow")  # Animated choropleth over a year panel: needs `gganimate` world_data(2000:2020, c(gdp = "NY.GDP.PCAP.KD")) |>   animate_world(gdp)  # Interactive choropleth: needs `leaflet`, `ggiraph` or `plotly` world_data(2020) |>   interactive_map(gdp_per_capita, engine = "plotly")

title: The comparative-development toolkit
text: Milanovic separates inequality countries units (concept 1) inequality countries weighted populations (concept 2). inequality() gives every standard measure either: much lies continents? Theil’s L decomposes without depending order:
code: inequality(snap$gdp_per_capita) #> # A tibble: 7 × 2 #>   measure   value #>   <chr>     <dbl> #> 1 gini      0.638 #> 2 theil_t   0.746 #> 3 theil_l   0.916 #> 4 atkinson  0.600 #> 5 cv        1.54  #> 6 palma     9.36  #> 7 p90_p10  43.7 inequality(snap$gdp_per_capita, weights = snap$population) #> # A tibble: 7 × 2 #>   measure   value #>   <chr>     <dbl> #> 1 gini      0.612 #> 2 theil_t   0.686 #> 3 theil_l   0.774 #> 4 atkinson  0.539 #> 5 cv        1.40  #> 6 palma     7.70  #> 7 p90_p10  32.7 theil(snap$gdp_per_capita, snap$population, groups = snap$continent, type = "L") #> # A tibble: 3 × 3 #>   component value share #>   <chr>     <dbl> <dbl> #> 1 total     0.774 1     #> 2 between   0.349 0.451 #> 3 within    0.425 0.549

title: The comparative-development toolkit
text: beta_convergence() sigma_convergence() summarise distribution one number . transition_matrix() shows countries move within (Quah):
code: set.seed(4) pan <- expand.grid(iso3c = snap$iso3c[1:60], year = 2000:2010,                    stringsAsFactors = FALSE) pan$gdp <- exp(9 + stats::ave(stats::rnorm(nrow(pan), 0, 0.05), pan$iso3c,                               FUN = cumsum) + rep(stats::rnorm(60), 11)) tm <- transition_matrix(pan, gdp, n_classes = 3, classes = "relative") tm #> # A tibble: 9 × 4 #>    from    to     n      p #>   <int> <int> <int>  <dbl> #> 1     1     1   189 0.940  #> 2     2     1    12 0.0594 #> 3     3     1     0 0      #> 4     1     2    12 0.0597 #> 5     2     2   180 0.891  #> 6     3     2     5 0.0254 #> 7     1     3     0 0      #> 8     2     3    10 0.0495 #> 9     3     3   192 0.975 attr(tm, "ergodic") #> [1] 0.2521957 0.2534504 0.4943538 rank_mobility(pan, gdp, from = 2000, to = 2010) #> # A tibble: 1 × 4 #>       n   tau  p_value share_moved #>   <int> <dbl>    <dbl>       <dbl> #> 1    60 0.879 3.27e-23       0.217

title: countryatlas and ggsql
text: world_query() pure string builder (needs nothing installed), can see exactly sent ggsql:
code: world_query(   gdp_per_capita,   projection = "equal_earth",   palette    = "magma",   transform  = "log10",   title      = "GDP per capita" ) #> VISUALISE gdp_per_capita AS fill #> FROM countryatlas_world #> DRAW spatial #> PROJECT TO equal_earth #> SCALE fill TO magma VIA log10 #> LABEL title => 'GDP per capita'

title: countryatlas and ggsql
text: as_ggsql_source() exports curated countryatlas table (sf geometry WKB-encoded) DuckDB connection, Parquet file, nanoarrow stream ggsql can read. one-call path interactive_map(engine = "ggsql"): hood just two building blocks, can also drive full control query:
code: # needs: ggsql, duckdb, DBI, sf world_data(2020, geometry = "sf") |>   interactive_map(gdp_per_capita, engine = "ggsql", transform = "log10") src <- world_data(2020, geometry = "sf") |>   as_ggsql_source(format = "duckdb")          # a DuckDB connection  q <- world_query(gdp_per_capita, projection = "orthographic", palette = "viridis")  ggsql::ggsql_execute(src, q)                  # -> Vega-Lite widget

title: countryatlas and ggsql
text: Loading ggsql registers chunk engine. Export source , chart ```{ggsql} block, referencing registered table name:
code: ```{r} library(countryatlas) library(ggsql)  src <- world_data(2020, geometry = "sf") |>   as_ggsql_source(format = "duckdb")          # registers countryatlas_world ```  ```{ggsql connection=src} VISUALISE gdp_per_capita AS fill FROM countryatlas_world DRAW spatial PROJECT TO equal_earth SCALE fill TO magma VIA log10 LABEL title => 'GDP per capita, 2020' ```

title: countryatlas: Joining World Data to Maps on the ISO Spine
text: Joining country-level data across independent sources deceptively hard: country spelled "US", "U.S.", "United States" "United States America", naïve join treats different entities. countryatlas resolves friction adopting ISO 3166 codes universal join key stitching together three otherwise disjoint resources (map geometry, World Bank development indicators, comprehensive country-code crosswalk) single, map-ready table. vignette presents package’s design philosophy, core functional vocabulary, worked examples spanning data assembly, join engine, diagnostics, reference data, analysis helpers grammar honest cartographic displays; companion vignettes take remaining map types, projections query interface detail. examples run offline bundled data snapshot.

title: countryatlas: Joining World Data to Maps on the ISO Spine
text: package rests single conviction: task make easier get country data onto map, make map honest, belong . Concretely, three packages combined: Natural Earth, bundled 1:50m (sf three scales), supplies polygon geometry, .e. countries ; WDI supplies World Bank indicators, .e. true ; countrycode supplies crosswalk ISO codes, continents regions makes reliable join possible. Three design commitments follow. First, happy path one call: world_data(2020) returns tibble ready map. Second, ISO code spine: every function speaks iso3c/iso2c internally exposes , anything package produces joins anything else, user’s data. Third, country lost silently: entities map backends spell idiosyncratically matched curated override table rather dropped, unmatched values reported explicitly. keep every example reproducible without network connection, vignette uses bundled world_snapshot dataset, curated set indicators one recent year.

title: countryatlas: join World Bank data, country codes and maps on the ISO spine — countryatlas-package
text: Eight options change package's behaviour. unset default. countryatlas.cache_dir persistent cache lives, one directory per source. Defaults tools::R_user_dir("countryatlas", "cache"); set "" session-caching. See clear_country_cache(). countryatlas.cache_max_age long persistent cache entry stays usable, seconds. Defaults 30 days. World Bank figures revised, old entry merely stale disk – different answer one API give now. single non-negative number; Inf expiry. countryatlas.cache_max_size size cap persistent cache, bytes. Defaults 50 MB, past least-recently-used entries dropped. CRAN policy allows package cache tools::R_user_dir() contents actively managed. single non-negative number; Inf cap. countryatlas.workers many processes fetch indicators parallel (cache disk – memory-memo survive fork). Defaults one fewer available cores, 2 R CMD check, per CRAN policy. Must single finite number; values one clamped one. countryatlas.timeout long one request provider may take, seconds. Defaults 60. Every built-source goes client, failing fetch bounded: countryatlas.retries + 1 requests length , plus waits . countryatlas.retries many times request retried failure worth retrying (HTTP 429, 5xx, dropped connection), exponential backoff jitter, honouring Retry-. Defaults 3; whole number 0 10. countryatlas.strict Set TRUE make failed download error (class countryatlas_fetch_failed) instead warning empty result, pipeline must continue data missing. default, FALSE, CRAN asks package uses network: fail gracefully. countryatlas.dispute_policy map convention disputed territories drawn : "none" (default), "de_facto", "de_jure" "neutral". Set dispute_policy() rather directly, also reports setting change. countryatlas.worldview Natural Earth point view sf backend draws, viewing country's ISO code ("IND") "ISO"; unset default. Set dispute_policy(worldview = ), validates ; see world_geometry().

title: Geary's C (spatial autocorrelation) — gearys_c
text: classical global autocorrelation statistic. Moran's correlation-like measure centred \(-1/(n-1)\), Geary's C distance-like one centred 1: 1 means positive autocorrelation (neighbours similar), 1 means negative. sensitive Moran's local differences.

title: Geary's C (spatial autocorrelation) — gearys_c
text: data country-level frame iso3c value column. value value column (unquoted). weights country_weights() object. NULL (default) uses country_weights("knn", k = 5): every country's five nearest neighbours, islands included. country_weights("contiguity") gives land-border default earlier versions, leaves every island . n_perm Permutations pseudo-p-value (default 999; use 0 skip test, leaves p_value NA).

title: Geary's C (spatial autocorrelation) — gearys_c
text: one-row tibble: c (observed), expected (always 1), n (countries used), n_excluded (countries data weights reach), n_links (non-zero weights), p_value excluded list-column excluded iso3c codes. n n_excluded sum countries supplied value, mean morans_i(). p_value one-sided lower tail: \((1 + \#\{C^{*} \le C_{obs}\}) / (n_{perm} + 1)\). lower tail clustered one, opposite way round Moran's : Geary's C runs 0 (neighbours identical) 1 (autocorrelation) upwards, small c evidence positive spatial association. Never exactly zero; floor \(1/(n_{perm}+1)\). Set seed beforehand reproducible p_value.

title: Geary's C (spatial autocorrelation) — gearys_c

title: Local Moran's I (LISA) — local_morans
text: local statistic runs one test per country, 190 , alpha = 0.05 roughly ten countries expected look significant nothing going . p_adjust = "fdr" controls false discovery rate instead – share flagged countries false alarms – standard remedy exactly setting (Caldas de Castro & Singer 2006) GeoDa offers. "bonferroni" "holm" control chance false alarm, stricter; "none" reproduces unadjusted labels earlier versions. p_value never adjusted, still matches spdep. Adjustment needs resolution. permutation p-value go \(1/(n_{perm}+1)\), Benjamini-Hochberg flags significant 190 tests p-value \(0.05/190 \approx 0.00026\). 999 permutations floor, 0.001, , nothing short several countries reaching floor can flagged, empty map say "clusters" means "enough permutations". Hence default 9,999, takes second whole world. p_value two-sided pseudo-p conditional permutation: \((1 + \#\{|I_i^{*}| \ge |I_i|\}) / (n_{perm} + 1)\), never exactly zero floor \(1/(n_{perm}+1)\) – default 999 permutations, 0.001. Two-sided local statistic interesting ends: country surrounded unlike neighbours much finding one surrounded like ones. cluster "significant" wherever p_value > alpha, everywhere n_perm = 0 leaves NA. Set seed beforehand reproducible p_value.

what: Theil index, with between/within decomposition — theil
title: Theil index, with between/within decomposition — theil
text: Theil inequality indices – less famous Gini, decompose exactly -group within-group component, answering "much world inequality continents vs within ?" one call. Weight population describe inequality people rather country units. type = "T" (default) Theil's T, weighted income shares; type = "L" Theil's L, mean log deviation, weighted population shares, whose decomposition path-independent.

title: Theil index, with between/within decomposition — theil

title: Theil index, with between/within decomposition — theil
text: x positive numeric vector (log scale; zero/negative values dropped warning). weights Optional non-negative weights (e.g. population), either length x length 1. groups Optional grouping vector (e.g. continent), length x (length 1). supplied, decomposition returned instead scalar. row whose group missing dropped along rows whose value missing, decomposition's total computed grouped subset can differ ungrouped theil(x). na.rm Whether drop NA values (default TRUE). type "T" (default) "L". T \(\sum_i s_i (x_i/\mu)   \log(x_i/\mu)\) population shares \(s_i\); L \(\sum_i s_i   \log(\mu/x_i)\). decompositions differ: T's within-group term weights group share income, L's share population, L's within parts depend order taken .

title: countryatlas 4.0.0
